name: Slysh haloes: the waste heat of cold computing as a submillimetre technosignature
summary: Michael Garrett's preprint models cold, distributed computing radiators as a partial Dyson swarm and proposes archival and targeted searches for their far-infrared or submillimetre waste heat while emphasizing natural-source discrimination.

publicationMetadata.publicationStatus: Scientific preprint submitted to MNRAS; peer review and acceptance not established

researchLibraryMetadata.methodology: Combines Landauer scaling, thermal-equilibrium and radiator-area arguments with modeled spectral emission, archival survey sensitivity, six observational discriminants and a proposed three-tier search program.
researchLibraryMetadata.principalFindings: Cold computing in the approximate 5–30 K regime could shift hypothetical waste heat into far-infrared and submillimetre bands. Archival nearby-star surveys may constrain cold circumstellar dissipation near 10^20 W under the model, with M dwarfs highlighted as favorable targets.
researchLibraryMetadata.limitations: The architecture and civilization behavior are hypothetical; diffuse emission may be faint; detectability depends on temperature, luminosity, geometry, distance and instrument response; cold dust, debris, galaxies, spectral-line sources and instrumental effects can mimic parts of the signature.
researchLibraryMetadata.researchImplication: Existing archives and targeted observations can test a colder region of Dysonian waste-heat parameter space, and null results can constrain the modeled class.

evidenceRecords.finding: The minimum energy cost of irreversible computation scales with temperature.
Temperature, luminosity and radiator area define the predicted far-infrared/submillimetre phase space.
DEBRIS, DUNES, SONS, Planck, JCMT, ALMA and NOEMA observations are proposed as search or constraint resources.
Six observational tests are assembled to separate modeled engineered radiators from natural cold sources.
The paper outlines survey reinterpretation, archival reprocessing and targeted follow-up as a staged search program.

editorialNotes.noDetection: No Slysh halo or extraterrestrial technology was detected or claimed.
editorialNotes.modelDiscipline: The 5–30 K range, approximately 10^20 W archival sensitivity and example detectability distances are scenario-dependent model outputs, not universal thresholds.
editorialNotes.naturalAlternatives: Cold circumstellar material and background or instrumental sources must be excluded before technological interpretation.
editorialNotes.publicationDiscipline: MNRAS submission does not establish peer review, acceptance or journal publication.
